title: Parasite Features: Causal Abstraction Through Spurious Pathways
abstract: arXiv:2611.26711v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Causal Abstraction defines a notion of \emph{equivalence} between a neural network and an algorithm, thus serving as a powerful framework for mechanistic interpretability. In this paper, however, we show the existence of a class of \emph{spurious features} which straightforwardly pass such equivalence tests. Suppose there are two directions in a model's representation space where: (i) one discriminates the input based on some feature, and (ii) the other steers the model towards a certain output. Interpretability methods based on Causal Abstraction (e.g., Distributed Alignment Search) can \emph{spuriously} simulate these directions' combined behavior by leveraging pathways passing through them, giving the impression that the model implements this feature. In such cases, we say the method discovered a \defn{parasite feature}. Experimentally, we show that Distributed Alignment Search finds parasite features using linear alignment maps in tw

translated_title: 寄生特征：经由虚假路径的因果抽象
translated_abstract: 因果抽象定义了神经网络与算法之间的一种“等价”概念，因此成为机械可解释性的一个强大框架。然而，本文展示了一类能够直接通过此类等价性检验的“虚假特征”的存在。假设模型的表示空间中存在两个方向：其中一个基于某种特征对输入进行判别，另一个则引导模型产生某个特定输出。基于因果抽象的可解释性方法（例如分布式对齐搜索，Distributed Alignment Search）可以通过利用经过这些方向的路径来“虚假地”模拟这些方向的联合行为，从而给人留下模型实现了该特征的印象。在这种情况下，我们称该方法发现了一个“寄生特征”。在实验中，我们展示了分布式对齐搜索利用线性对齐映射发现了寄生特征……
tldr: 论文揭示了一类“寄生特征”能够通过因果抽象的等价性检验，导致分布式对齐搜索等可解释性方法误认为模型实现了某种特征，暴露了该框架的盲点。
